newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end at record high as cyclicals shine.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end at record high as cyclicals shine.

text.p: 1610 GMT - Swiss shares came off intra-day peaks but still closed at record highs. Dealers said the market was split as banks were neglected while buying centred on cyclical shares.
* Broad SPI up 22.70 points to record close at 2,549.31 after touching an intra-day all-time high of 2,550.89.
* Blue-chip SMI up 28.1 to record close at 3,975.5 after an all-time high at 3,983.5 during the day.
Dealers said the market was waiting for Tuesday's U.S. December CPI figures.
The firm dollar and higher prices on Wall Street supported sentiment.
Banks were under some pressure from technical factors and because of the ongoing row over dormant Jewish wealth and looted Nazi gold, dealers said.
The technical factors included the options and futures expiry on Soffex an Friday, which coincide with several expiring warrants on UBS shares.
UBS lost 16 Swiss francs to 1,154. CS group rose 0.25 francs to 134.75. SBC shed 2.75 to 248.25.
Novartis, Roche and Nestle led the market higher. ABB gained nine francs to 1,655.
Among second-tier shares, EMS Chemie were stronger. Adecco, Schindler and Pirelli were also higher.
Phonak were lower. Kuoni and Gurit were also easier.

Trade on Soffex centred on roll-over transactions in banks ahead of Friday's expiry. Implicit volatility was decreasing. Index options were about 40 percent of total volume. In all 9,225 SMI futures were traded. The January SMI closed 38 points higher at 3,977 points.
